column1: # Level-1 route trace: the RETAIL-derived reference (issue #8).
# Same columns and the same fixed 600 ms sample ticks as `level1-route-port.tsv`
# (tick = 36 x 1/60 s; x/y/z are the player BODY position, the value retail's `coords` prints;
#  vel_x/vel_y/vel_z are the position derivative over the 600 ms sample window, in world units per second).
# `# epsilon` is this fixture's **stated tolerance**, in the trace's own units: the gate compares every
# numeric column against it (sector stays exact). It is the retail harness's resolution, not a parity
# slack: a 600 ms hold advances a variable amount of engine time (2-4 frames of the engine's [10,500] ms
# clock, plus the first segment's window-activation wait with the key already down), so one sample's
# displacement varies by up to a full sample of travel — 0.9 units at level 1's 0.875 u/s, and 1.5 u/s
# once that displacement is divided by the 600 ms window into the velocity columns. The port advances
# exactly 600 ms of game time per row, so the residual is that quantisation. Two retail captures of the
# cantina leg already disagree by 0.18 units and by a sector at 1.8 s.
# epsilon 1.70
# Provenance: the retail half of issue #8's scripted route, captured in ONE game session by
# `retail-capture.ps1 -RouteWalk` (2026-11-09). Four independent leg captures each started from a fresh
# level load, so their bars carried different pre-warp damage and could not be compared. A `warp` row
# runs the console warp at its tick, an `input` row holds forward for its ticks in 600 ms segments, and
# every segment ends with a console read that freezes the game between holds (the committed walk
# traces' methodology, so the pre-pressed key cannot move the body outside the measured window).
# Positions, sector and velocity are the committed walk traces' samples, as before
# (`spawn-walk.tsv`, `walk_cantina-walk.tsv`, `walk_street45-walk.tsv`, `walk_door0-walk.tsv`); the
# bars and cogs come from the continuous capture.
# `-` means the committed retail capture did not record that field. This reference has none: the
# bars and both cogs are captured. Health/shields are read from the retail engine's memory at every
# segment end (`thing+0x134` and inventory bin 60, the same reads the door telemetry uses); both cogs
# are read with `cogstatus 0` and `cogstatus 11` after each leg. Both cogs report all four fields zero
# wherever they were read (`doorstatus`/`movestatus`/`opendoors`/`closedoors` for cog 0,
# `doorstatus`/`movestatus`/`open_doors`/`close_doors` for cog 11).
# Retail does not survive the route: the cantina ambush drops the player from 100/100 to 0/0 between
# ticks 180 and 252 in the captured run, so the bars after the death are the engine's dead-player zeros
# and the body stops moving (the warps still reposition it at each leg). The gate reports that
# divergence instead of skipping it; it is a retail-vs-port combat difference, not a capture gap.
# A leg boundary (tick 180/324/504) is the next leg's warp pose, exactly as `walk-shots.tsv` names
# it; the previous leg's last 600 ms sample is therefore replaced by the new leg's start row.
